outcomes.title: Design a counterexample · Case explained · 1.4
outcomes.source: Review case: A river remains in both drawings while a workshop appears. What belongs in the changed column? Proposed answer: “The river vanished.”. Method note: Make rows for crossing, buildings and land cover, then columns for before and after. lessons.title: Review and repair: Mistake clinic · Locate the UK at island and country scales / Mistake clinic · Explain relief rainfall as a connected process

outcomes.title: Mistake clinic · Case explained · 3.1
outcomes.source: Review case: Which statement places Northern Ireland correctly? Proposed answer: “Part of Great Britain, east of England.”. Method note: Great Britain is the island containing England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is on the island of Ireland and is also part of the UK. Start with the islands, then add country names and surrounding waters.

outcomes.title: Change the example · 3.1
outcomes.source: Map reference: the UK includes England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Great Britain contains England, Scotland and Wales. The island of Ireland contains Northern Ireland and Ireland. North Sea: east of Great Britain; Irish Sea: between the islands.

outcomes.title: Mistake clinic · Case explained · 3.3
outcomes.source: Review case: The incoming air becomes much drier. What prediction follows, other things equal? Proposed answer: “The mountain creates the missing water.”. Method note: Moist air rises over high ground and cools. Condensation can form cloud and precipitation. Descending air on the other side may be drier; wind and moisture supply matter, so a mountain does not guarantee rain every day.

outcomes.title: Design a counterexample · Case explained · 3.3
outcomes.source: Review case: The incoming air becomes much drier. What prediction follows, other things equal? Proposed answer: “The mountain creates the missing water.”. outcomes.source: Review case: Which item is an impact rather than a cause of flooding? Proposed answer: “Heavy rainfall.”. Method note: Heavy rain on saturated soil may increase rapid runoff; flow exceeding channel capacity may flood homes. “Wet weather → damage” skips the mechanism. Separate the cause, pathway and consequence.

outcomes.title: Mistake clinic · Case explained · 5.8
outcomes.source: Review case: Rain is 40 units and infiltration 25%. How much is model runoff? Proposed answer: “10 units.”. Method note: In a simplified 20-unit rainfall trial, 60% infiltration means 12 infiltrate and 8 run off. At 30%, 6 infiltrate and 14 run off. Keep rainfall fixed to isolate infiltration's effect; the model omits storage and timing.

outcomes.title: Change the example · 5.8

outcomes.title: Mistake clinic · Case explained · 5.9
outcomes.source: Review case: A local drain is blocked after rain. What directly addresses that blockage? Proposed answer: “Assume a distant tidal barrier clears it.”. Method note: A tidal barrier addresses incoming high water at its protected location; it does not remove every upstream rainfall or drainage problem. Warnings help preparation, while drainage work addresses a different pathway.

outcomes.title: Mistake clinic · Case explained · 5.10
outcomes.source: Review case: A package costs 25 + 20 + 15 tokens with a budget of 50. Is it feasible? Proposed answer: “Yes; each item individually costs less than 50.”. Method note: With 50 tokens, a 10-token warning system and 30-token storage area cost 40, leaving 10. Warnings help people respond; storage may hold water. Neither guarantees zero harm in every event.
